title: autotune: defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles and unit-econ tooling
author: Jordan Meyers
release_notes: Introduce autotune defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, add recommended quantization profiles for common model families, and ship initial unit-economics (UEcon) CLI and dashboard metrics. Backward compatible; operators can opt into new defaults per-deployment.
description: Motivation: reduce per-token cost while preserving latency SLOs and output quality. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) runtime defaults and autotune rules for batching and KV-prefix caching to favor slightly higher batching thresholds under steady-state traffic while preserving tail latency via aggressive latency SLO checks; 2) a quantization profile registry and selection heuristics (int8-fp32 hybrid and AWQ-style 4-bit) with safe fallbacks for models that fail accuracy gates; 3) unit-economics tooling (UEcon) including a CLI and backend endpoints to compute per-route per-token cost estimates and surface suggested config changes. The description below is a continuous summary and includes rollout guidance, test results, and operator notes. Checklist: [x] design review (ENG-3129) [x] perf bench (canary) [x] integration tests [x] docs and release notes [x] canary rollout plan. Rollout guidance: deploy feature branch to canary region A, enable new defaults in non-critical routing (10% traffic), monitor metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, memory pressure, model quality via eval set; if quality regressions appear revert quant profile or pin model to previous profile. UEcon usage: run `redwood-uecon estimate --route <route-id> --window 24h` to see per-token unit cost and suggested savings; the tool outputs human-readable suggestions and a JSON payload for the Console to apply. Backwards compatibility: defaults are opt-in for Dedicated and Private; hosted customers receive opt-out toggles. Related work: ENG-3180 autotune infra improvements, PM-211 product acceptance criteria. Notes: this PR contains small runtime kernel selection changes; any model-specific regressions must be caught by model-level evals before full rollout.

conversation: Priya Nair: Nice work. A few questions: 1) how do we guarantee we don't increase p99 latency when batching threshold increases? 2) where are the accuracy gates for quant profiles?

Jordan Meyers: Answered: the autotune uses a latency SLO monitor that prevents batching threshold increases past the point where p99 deviates by more than 7% relative to baseline; accuracy gates are implemented as a small eval set run during canary that compares BLEU/EM/semantic-similarity thresholds per model family. Added tests and thresholds in profiles_registry.go.
